# Atomic Factual Intents — Chapter 5B — AMLO 2022

**Source hash:** `8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80` (BOOK-013, CIDOB political biography)
**Role:** independent_reference biography
**Period scope:** material here primarily documents AMLO's *pre-presidential* platforms (2008–2018 campaigns), party founding, and opposition posture. The biographical narrative precedes and frames his 2018–2024 presidency; **period-fit for 2022 is indirect** (manifests intent, doctrine, and stated agenda; **not** documented execution of budgets, rules, or outcomes in 2022).

---

## D0001 — Type: program_intent
- **lens_id:** 5B.1
- **topic:** broad-based prosperity vs. rents in stated agenda
- **actor:** Andrés Manuel López Obrador (AMLO)
- **action:** articulated and re-iterated an economic program ("Proyecto Alternativo de Nación" / 2012 and 2018 programs) pledging "austeridad republicana" to redirect public resources from current spending to investment without raising taxes; "incluyente" 6% annual growth via public-private-social alliance; 1.2 million jobs/year; eradication of hunger and food self-sufficiency; minimum-wage growth above inflation; popular housing; universal public coverage in education, health, and pensions for adults ≥68 and persons with disabilities.
- **mechanism:** campaign platform / doctrinal program, not enacted legislation
- **outcome:** proposed (not executed within the routed passage)
- **dates:** program formulations 2010, 2012, and 2018
- **quantities:** 6% annual growth target; 1.2M jobs/year; pension age 68+
- **attribution:** CIDOB biographical narrative (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** positive (intent broadly aligned with broad-based prosperity; critics framed as rents-prone elsewhere)
- **period_fit:** **weak** for 2022 — documents *intent* pre-2022; no 2022 execution data
- **limitations:** no executed budget, no outcome data; platform text only
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.1
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 48, segments S00001–S00004 (inclusive); **and** extracted HTML block 5, segments S00001–S00002 (inclusive)

## D0002 — Type: program_intent
- **lens_id:** 5B.1
- **topic:** ending fiscal privileges / corruption as prosperity base
- **actor:** AMLO
- **action:** in 2010 platform speech at Zócalo, identified current economic policy as condemning Mexico to "atraso"; called for ending "privilegios fiscales" useless for growth and for strengthening Pemex via prospecting/refining investment to head off a looming petroleum-output crisis and gasoline import dependency of ~40%.
- **mechanism:** campaign rhetoric / programmatic proposal
- **outcome:** proposed
- **dates:** 25 July 2010 (Zócalo speech)
- **quantities:** 40% of consumed gasoline imported
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** negative diagnosis of incumbent policy; positive proposed remedy
- **period_fit:** weak for 2022 (pre-presidency speech)
- **limitations:** rhetorical; no implementation evidence
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.1
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 42, segments S00006–S00010 (inclusive)

## D0003 — Type: program_intent
- **lens_id:** 5B.1, 5B.3
- **topic:** energy-sector doctrine — state ownership, anti-privatization
- **actor:** AMLO
- **action:** pledged to "blindar la titularidad estatal de Pemex," place all hydrocarbon production/transformación at the exclusive service of the nation per the Constitution; explore and exploit all viable petroleum reserves; build three new refineries to cut imports; expand national human capital in petroleum; halt and reverse power-sector privatizations in generation, transmission, and distribution; promote renewable/alternative energies; ultimately reduce energy tariffs and prices.
- **mechanism:** doctrinal energy plank of "Proyecto Alternativo de Nación" (10-point decálogo, point 8: "El sector energético, palanca del desarrollo nacional")
- **outcome:** proposed
- **dates:** 2012 platform formulation
- **quantities:** three refineries
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** pro-state-control; framed by incumbents as costly / anti-modernizing
- **period_fit:** weak for 2022 (2012 campaign plank)
- **limitations:** doctrinal text, not executed legislation/budget
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.1; 5B.3
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 47, segments S00001–S00006 (inclusive); **and** extracted HTML block 46, segment S00011 (point 8 of decálogo)

## D0004 — Type: cabinet_intent
- **lens_id:** 5B.2
- **topic:** proposed senior economic / security appointees (qualifications, independence unspecified)
- **actor:** AMLO
- **action:** in 2012 campaign announced that his cabinet would include Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas (Pemex), Marcelo Ebrard (Secretaría de Gobernación), and Elena Poniatowska Amor (Secretaría de Cultura).
- **mechanism:** campaign promise
- **outcome:** proposed (not in power)
- **dates:** 2012 campaign
- **quantities:** three named positions
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** ambiguous — names recognized public figures; the passage does **not** document credible selection process, professional qualifications vetting, operational independence, or performance-based retention/replacement
- **period_fit:** not applicable for 2022 (these were 2012 hypotheticals; **not** a documented 2022 cabinet action)
- **limitations:** the passage does not show 5B.2 substantive criteria (process, independence, performance-based retention)
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.2
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 49, segment S00002

## D0005 — Type: party_org
- **lens_id:** 5B.2
- **topic:** MORENA founding executive — selection of internal officials
- **actor:** MORENA (under AMLO)
- **action:** 20 November 2014 National Congress of MORENA approved basic documents and elected: National Council with AMLO as president; National Executive Committee with Martí Batres Guadarrama (former Social Development Secretary of DF, federal PRD deputy) as president and Bertha Elena Luján Uranga (former Comptroller General of DF, FAT union) as secretary general; 204-person Council included Paco Ignacio Taibo II, Rosario Ibarra de Piedra, René Drucker Colín, Elena Poniatowska, Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, José Agustín Ortiz Pinchetti.
- **mechanism:** party-internal election
- **outcome:** party officers installed
- **dates:** 20 November 2014
- **quantities:** 204 Council members
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** neutral (internal-party process; the passage does **not** evaluate professional credentials, independence, or performance accountability)
- **period_fit:** pre-presidency (2014)
- **limitations:** party-internal selection, not a documented public-sector economic-appointment process; does **not** support 5B.2 substantive criteria
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.2 (weak/marginal support)
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 53, segments S00001–S00006 (inclusive)

## D0006 — Type: legislative_context
- **lens_id:** 5B.3, 5B.4
- **topic:** PRD internal defeat preceded a major energy reform enacted *without* AMLO
- **actor:** Mexican Congress (Calderón era); PRD factions ("Los Chuchos" and allies)
- **action:** October 2008 — Congress approved a package of seven decree-laws establishing the Comisión Nacional de Hidrocarburos as Pemex regulator and facilitating renegotiation of exploitation contracts on allegedly more advantageous fiscal terms; PRI, PAN, PVEM, and a PRD faction associated with Los Chuchos combined to pass it; FAP sabotage tactics failed.
- **mechanism:** legislative vote combining PAN-PRI-PVEM and dissident PRD
- **outcome:** reform approved; PRD fractured; FAP legislators lost on the decisive Senate vote; the "Movimiento Nacional en Defensa del Petróleo" civil-resistance mobilization could not block the Senate vote
- **dates:** October 2008 (approval); 2009 federal legislative election cost the PRD (5 July 2009 — fell to 12.2% of vote, −54 deputies, total 72)
- **quantities:** seven decree-laws; PRD share drop to 12.2%; −54 deputies
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** describes a Calderón-era reform *opposed* by AMLO; relevant as context for AMLO's later energy doctrine
- **period_fit:** **out of scope** for 2022 (Calderón presidency, 2008–2009)
- **limitations:** contextual background only; not a 2022 act
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.3; 5B.4 (contextual)
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 41, segments S00009–S00014 (inclusive)

## D0007 — Type: rule_position
- **lens_id:** 5B.3, 5B.4
- **topic:** AMLO opposition to Peña Nieto structural reforms (energy, telecoms, education, labor)
- **actor:** AMLO / MORENA
- **action:** rejected the Pacto por México (signed 2 December 2012) and the subsequent structural reforms in energy (which ended Pemex and CFE monopoly regimes), telecommunications, education, and labor; argued energy reform carried privatizing intent despite government assertions that state ownership of oil and gas remained intact.
- **mechanism:** political opposition / doctrinal rejection
- **outcome:** MORENA outside the consensus; no documented enacted rule by AMLO in this period
- **dates:** December 2012 onward
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** negative (rejection) toward incumbent reforms
- **period_fit:** **out of scope** for 2022 (2012–2014 opposition)
- **limitations:** passage documents opposition, **not** AMLO's own enacted fiscal/monetary/financial rules
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.3; 5B.4
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 53, segments S00009–S00011 (inclusive); **and** extracted HTML block 54, segments S00001–S00006 (inclusive)

## D0008 — Type: rhetoric_position
- **lens_id:** 5B.5
- **topic:** anti-corruption rhetoric and proposed instruments
- **actor:** AMLO (2012 candidate)
- **action:** promised to "limpiar al Gobierno como a las escaleras, de arriba abajo" with requisite anti-corruption instruments and bodies; investigations would include FOBAPROA and Pemex via truth commissions; pledged *no* persecution of individuals.
- **mechanism:** campaign promise
- **outcome:** proposed
- **dates:** 2012 campaign
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** positive rhetoric; no execution documented here
- **period_fit:** weak for 2022 (campaign text only)
- **limitations:** no documented enforcement against politically connected actors, no audit/court cooperation, no remedy of favoritism or capture
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.5
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 46, segments S00006–S00008 (inclusive)

## D0009 — Type: program_intent
- **lens_id:** 5B.6
- **topic:** budget/investment redirection — austerity republicana
- **actor:** AMLO (2018 Proyecto)
- **action:** proposed "austeridad republicana" to redirect public resources from current expenditures to investment without raising taxes; also aimed to increase domestic gasoline supply to cut imports and lower prices; pursued energy and food self-sufficiency with guaranteed prices for agricultural producers.
- **mechanism:** 2018 campaign program for "Juntos Haremos Historia" coalition (MORENA, PT, PES)
- **outcome:** proposed
- **dates:** 2018 program
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** positive (intent)
- **period_fit:** **weak for 2022** (2018 platform)
- **limitations:** the passage records platform text only — does **not** document actual 2022 executed budgets, infrastructure delivery, or administrative-capacity outcomes
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.6
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 5, segments S00001, S00003–S00007 (inclusive)

## D0010 — Type: party_rhetoric
- **lens_id:** 5B.7
- **topic:** "regeneration" doctrine and public-information posture
- **actor:** AMLO / MORENA
- **action:** in 2012 candidacy and 2018 program articulated a "regeneración ética y moral" / "revolución de las conciencias" framework; the 10-point "Diez puntos para el renacimiento de México" included (1) revolution of consciousness / critical thinking; (2) state at the service of people and nation; (3) democratize media access; (4) republican ethics and anti-corruption; (5) new economy; (6) combat monopolies; (7) abolish fiscal privileges to redistribute wealth with justice; (8) energy sector as development lever; (9) countryside and food sovereignty; (10) welfare state and right to happiness.
- **mechanism:** doctrinal program / rhetoric
- **outcome:** proposed
- **dates:** 2012 (program) / reaffirmed 2018
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** positive (stated intent regarding transparency/ethics)
- **period_fit:** weak for 2022 (doctrinal statements; no documented 2022 audit cooperation, program correction, or independent-evaluation acceptance)
- **limitations:** no documented 2022 publication of reliable economic information, independent evaluation/audit cooperation, or correction of failed programs
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.7
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 46, segments S00008–S00011 (inclusive)

## D0011 — Type: program_intent
- **lens_id:** 5B.8
- **topic:** distributive agenda — fair distribution / welfare state
- **actor:** AMLO
- **action:** pledged to abolish fiscal privileges to redistribute wealth "with justice"; raise minimum wages above inflation; launch a popular housing program; extend universal public coverage in education (including university), health, and pensions to all adults ≥68 and persons with disabilities; combat monopolies; build a welfare state ("Estado de Bienestar y el derecho a la felicidad").
- **mechanism:** 10-point program (points 5, 7, 10 explicitly; reinforced in 2018)
- **outcome:** proposed
- **dates:** 2012 program; reinforced 2018
- **quantities:** pension age ≥68; minimum wage "above inflation"
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** positive (intent for cross-class fair distribution)
- **period_fit:** weak for 2022 (program text)
- **limitations:** no incidence data across classes/regions/genders documented in this passage
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.8
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 46, segments S00009–S00011 (inclusive); **and** extracted HTML block 48, segments S00001–S00004 (inclusive)

## D0012 — Type: party_founding
- **lens_id:** 5B.7 (marginal), 5B.10 (context)
- **topic:** MORENA doctrinal self-description
- **actor:** AMLO / MORENA
- **action:** defined MORENA as a political organization "amplia, plural, incluyente y de izquierda" with the stated objective of "luchar por un cambio de régimen" against an "oligárquico y conservador" power rooted in 1970s PRI administrations and continuing through PAN governments; diagnosed prior liberalization as having "legalized plunder" and privatized 26% of national territory.
- **mechanism:** party-founding rhetoric
- **outcome:** stated position
- **dates:** 2012–2014
- **quantities:** "26% del territorio nacional" characterized as privatized
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** strongly negative characterization of prior regime
- **period_fit:** pre-presidency; weak for 2022
- **limitations:** rhetorical / foundational; not documented 2022 economic-information transparency practice
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.7; 5B.10 (context)
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 44, segments S00005–S00010 (inclusive)

## D0013 — Type: opposition_event
- **lens_id:** 5B.9 (marginal)
- **topic:** AMLO's framing of economic crisis and Calderón-era "descomposición social"
- **actor:** AMLO (candidate, 2010 Zócalo speech)
- **action:** blamed the Calderón government for a "descomposición social" that had driven Mexico "to one of the worst crises in its history"; called for changing the current economic policy and ending useless fiscal privileges.
- **mechanism:** campaign diagnosis / shock framing
- **outcome:** proposed (policy change)
- **dates:** 25 July 2010
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** negative diagnosis; positive proposed remedy
- **period_fit:** **out of scope** for 2022 (2010 speech)
- **limitations:** no documentation of 2022 AMLO-government shock-response measures, targeting, monitoring, or correction

## D0014 — Type: security_econ_link
- **lens_id:** 5B.10
- **topic:** social-causes framing of violence — economic-development linkage
- **actor:** AMLO (2012 candidate)
- **action:** diagnosed organized-crime violence as rooted in social injustice, underdevelopment, exclusion, and structural corruption; called for "moralizing" police and security civil service (especially Policía Federal) and, after that, a gradual withdrawal of the Army from public-security roles (demilitarization of the anti-narco fight).
- **mechanism:** security-and-development policy linkage in campaign platform
- **outcome:** proposed
- **dates:** 2012 campaign
- **quantities:** "más de 50.000 muertos desde 2006" (cumulative body count cited as background)
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** pro-social-causes / anti-coercive-only approach
- **period_fit:** weak for 2022 (2012 platform; violence count cited as 2006–2012 background)
- **limitations:** the passage documents *intent and doctrine*; **no documented 2022 economic-trajectory outcome data** (lagged effects, institutional constraints, distributional outcomes, durability)
- **methodology_ids:** ruler-quality-questions-v1 / 5B.10
- **locator_disposition:** extracted HTML block 47, segments S00007–S00010 (inclusive); **and** extracted HTML block 46, segment S00005 (the 50,000-dead figure)

## D0015 — Type: party_registration
- **lens_id:** (no direct 5B lens; contextual)
- **topic:** MORENA party registration — formal political-organizational act
- **actor:** MORENA / AMLO
- **action:** on 9 July 2014, amid a verbal war between López Obrador and Zambrano over "traición" and division of the Mexican left, MORENA obtained its registration as a political party from the Instituto Nacional Electoral (INE).
- **mechanism:** INE registration
- **outcome:** MORENA became a registered national party
- **dates:** 9 July 2014
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** neutral procedural fact
- **period_fit:** pre-presidency
- **limitations:** party-organizational fact, not an economic-policy execution fact; do **not** map to 5B lenses beyond context
- **methodology_ids:** not mapped to any 5B.* lens (contextual only)

## D0016 — Type: election_outcome
- **lens_id:** (no direct 5B lens; contextual)
- **topic:** 2012 election result — second-place finish, contested
- **actor:** IFE / Mexican electorate / AMLO
- **action:** the IFE rapid count (PREP) gave Peña Nieto 37.93–38.55%; AMLO placed second with "algo más del 31%"; final cómputo (8 July 2012) confirmed Peña Nieto at 38.2% and AMLO at 31.57% — an absolute gap of 3.3 million ballots; AMLO declared the election "inequitativa y plagada de irregularidades," accused the PRI of a massive "compra de votos" operation and Peña Nieto of receiving "dinero ilícito" from the United States, and announced on 3 July 2012 that he would contest the election.
- **mechanism:** electoral process and post-electoral challenge
- **outcome:** Peña Nieto confirmed as president-elect; AMLO in second place
- **dates:** 1 July 2012 (vote); 3 July 2012 (AMLO contestation); 8 July 2012 (final cómputo)
- **quantities:** Peña Nieto 38.2%; AMLO 31.57%; gap 3.3 million votes
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** contested
- **period_fit:** **out of scope** for 2022
- **limitations:** not an economic-policy fact; contextual background only
- **methodology_ids:** not mapped to any 5B.* lens (contextual only)

## D0017 — Type: internal_party_event
- **lens_id:** (no direct 5B lens; contextual)
- **topic:** 2008 PRD internal election crisis — fragmented party discipline on economic reform vote
- **actor:** PRD (López Obrador / Marcelo Ebrard backing Alejandro Encinas vs. party apparatus backing Jesús Ortega); TEPJF
- **action:** chaotic 16 March 2008 internal election for CEN president; mutual fraud accusations; 19 July annulment by Comisión Nacional de Garantías y Vigilancia; Ortega's TEPJF appeal succeeded on 12 November; Ortega took oath as PRD president on 29 November.
- **mechanism:** internal party dispute adjudicated by TEPJF
- **outcome:** Ortega installed as PRD president; PRD lost legislative cohesion on the subsequent October 2008 energy reform
- **dates:** 16 March 2008; 19 July 2008; 12 November 2008; 29 November 2008
- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
- **polarity:** contested
- **period_fit:** **out of scope** for 2022

- **lens_id:** (no direct 5B lens; contextual)
- **topic:** 2010–2011 opposition coalition stance
- **actor:** AMLO / PRD
- **action:** rejected any PRD alliance with PAN in Estado de México (10 April 2011 PRD Consejo Nacional decision); argued PRI and PAN were "lo mismo" despite their mutual fighting; framed MORENA's purpose as regime change against a self-perpetuating PRI/PAN "alternancia."

- **dates:** 10 April 2011; 2 October 2011

- **attribution:** CIDOB (BOOK-013)
